To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high mass resolution MALDI–MSI is a powerful tool for visualizing and analyzing the spatial distribution of metabolite and lipid changes in plant roots in response to abiotics stress.

we used a combination approach of LC–MS, ICP–MS, and MALDI–MSI platforms to profile the spatial distribution of metabolite, lipid and ion composition in young developing barley roots before and after a 24 h salt stress (150 m mM NaCl).

the use of high-mass-resolution MALDIMS imaging in combination with LCMS, ICPMS and bioinformatics analysis can be used to study plant responses to salinity at the metabolite and lipid level in a spatially resolved manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the spatial distribution of metabolite profiles in the roots of barley seedling before and after salt treatment, which was achieved through the application of a combination of mass spectrometry techniques, including LC–MS, MALDI–MS, ICP–MS, which enabled the identification and localization of ions, metabolite and lipid composition in fine detail along the longitudinal root section and comparison of the profiles before and after salt treatments.
the spatial profiling of metabolites and elements in barley roots in response to salt stress and the use of mass spectrometry as a tool to study plant stress responses.
the development of novel analytical tools and methods for the study of the spatial distribution and localization of metabolites in plants and their responses to environmental stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work demonstrates the suitability of the combined approach for the study of plant roots and their response to abiotic stresses.
the combination of LC–MS, ICP–MS and MALDI–MSI is a powerful tool for the study of spatially resolved metabolic changes in response to salinization.

the use of a combination of mass spectrometry approaches is a powerful tool to investigate the physiological responses of plant roots to salinity stress, and that the use of MALDI-MSI can provide a detailed spatial distribution of lipids, ions, and metabolites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a combination of three mass spectrometric platforms can be used to study the spatial and temporal changes in the elemental, metabolic and lipid composition of roots in response to salinic stress.
we have shown that the use of three different mass spectrometry technologies can provide complementary information about plant roots in response to salinization.

this study has demonstrated that a multi-platform approach using MSI can be used to identify and visualize the spatial localization of metabolites and ions in roots in response to salt stress, and that the combination of LC–MS, MALDI–MSI, and ICP–MS can be used to study the physiological responses of plants to salinity stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spatial resolution of the mass spectrometry techniques used in this study allowed us to visualize and quantify changes in metabolites in response to salt stress, and to identify potential tolerance mechanisms.
the combination of the three platforms can provide comprehensive and detailed information about the spatial and compositional changes in roots in response to salt stress.
the use of high mass resolution MALDI–MSI can be used to study plant stress responses in fine detail and to identify the spatial distribution of metabolite profiles in response to stress.
